name: SSH allows root to sign in with a key
description: sshd accepts root with a public key (PermitRootLogin prohibit-password). Safer than a password, but it is a way in for anyone who gets that key and an account nobody can tell from another in the logs; most systems need only sudo.
message: sshd: PermitRootLogin prohibit-password (root signs in with a key)
remediation: Set PermitRootLogin no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and use a named account with sudo; keep it only for a job that needs it (backup, configuration management).
